# 1 Maccabees Chapter 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_016_page_001.jpg

---

**1** John came up from Gazara and reported to his father Simon what Cendebaeus had done.

**2** Simon summoned his two elder sons Judas and John and said to them: "My brothers and I and my father's house have fought the wars of Israel from our youth until this day, and it has been given to us to deliver Israel many times.

**3** But now I am old, and you, by God's mercy, are men of age. Take my place and my brother's place, and go out and fight for our nation; and may help from Heaven be with you."

**4** He mustered twenty thousand warriors and cavalry from the country, and they marched against Cendebaeus and spent the night at Modein.

**5** They set out in the morning and marched into the plain; a large army came to meet them — infantry and cavalry — and between them was a stream.

**6** John and his force drew up facing them for battle. Seeing that the soldiers were afraid to cross the stream, John crossed first; when the men saw this, they crossed after him.

**7** He divided the force and placed the cavalry in the middle of the infantry, for the enemy cavalry was very numerous.

**8** They sounded the trumpets, and Cendebaeus was routed; many of his men fell, and the rest fled into the stronghold.

**9** At that time Judas, the brother of John, was wounded; but John pressed the pursuit until Cendebaeus reached Kidron, which Cendebaeus himself had built.

**10** Some of the enemy fled into the towers in the fields of Azotus, and John burned it with fire; about two thousand of the enemy fell. He then returned to Judea in peace.

**11** Now Ptolemy son of Abubus had been appointed commander over the plain of Jericho, and he had accumulated much silver and gold,

**12** for he was the son-in-law of the high priest.

**13** His heart grew proud and he determined to make himself master of the country; he devised a treacherous plan to do away with Simon and his sons.

**14** Simon was making a tour of the cities of the country and attending to their needs when he came down to Jericho — he and his sons Mattathias and Judas — in the one hundred and seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month, which is the month of Shebat.

**15** The son of Abubus received them into a small stronghold called Dok, which he had built, with treachery; he prepared a great banquet for them and had men hidden there.

**16** When Simon and his sons had drunk deeply, Ptolemy and his men rose up, took their weapons, rushed upon Simon in the banqueting hall, and killed him along with his two sons and some of his servants.

**17** He committed a great act of treachery and repaid good with evil.

**18** Ptolemy wrote an account of all this and sent it to the king, asking him to send troops to help him and to hand over to him the country and the cities.

**19** He dispatched other men to Gazara to kill John, and sent letters to the commanders of thousands, inviting them to come to him and promising them silver, gold, and gifts.

**20** He also sent men to seize Jerusalem and the temple mount.

**21** But someone ran ahead and informed John at Gazara that his father and brothers had been killed, and that Ptolemy had sent men to kill him as well.

**22** When John heard this, he was greatly shaken; he seized the men who had come to kill him and put them to death, for he knew that they had come to take his life.

**23** As for the rest of the acts of John — his wars, his brave deeds, the walls he built, and all his achievements —

**24** these are recorded in the annals of his high priesthood, from the time he succeeded his father as high priest.
